audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gave Akshan five of seven stages (rows 0-3 and 6) while the content layer and the packet levelChart both gave Karma rows 0-3 and row 6. The page rendered opposite answers. The matchup was also labelled TRICKY at 7/10 difficulty against a 59.02% win rate over 61 games.
audit.why: Karma's Inner Flame is 950 range against Avengerang's 850, and Heroic Swing needs terrain to anchor to and is 18s at rank 1 — so the early lane genuinely belongs to Karma. Akshan's stages are 6 (Comeuppance, 100s, 2500 range, missing-health scaling) and his first item. Late, Comeuppance stops on the first champion, minion or structure it hits, which a wave supplies for free.
audit.corrected: Full-layer sides realigned to the content layer and the packet: Karma / Karma / Karma / Karma / Akshan / Akshan / Karma, with each why rewritten to match. diff moved from TRICKY to EVEN and diffRating 7/10 to 5/10 to stop the page arguing with its own win rate.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike ladder was intact but the level-6 and first-item spikes never named a cooldown, and the full-layer whys for those rows described Karma pressing an early lead — the opposite of the row's verdict.
audit.why: Comeuppance is 100/85/70s at 2500 range and deals damage based on missing health, which is what makes 6 his stage; his first item plus Heroic Swing off any wall is what makes the following one his.
audit.corrected: Rewrote phases[4].why and phases[5].why with the real numbers and the correct verdict; realigned content whys[5], which was still describing level 6 under the First-item row.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions never appeared anywhere on the page: Karma's W reveals Akshan out of Going Rogue, and Comeuppance is stopped by the first champion, minion or structure it hits.
audit.why: Riot's text on Focused Resolve says it deals damage and reveals the target; Going Rogue is camouflage. Riot's text on Comeuppance says the stored bullets damage the first champion, minion or structure hit — a minion between you and him eats the whole ultimate.
audit.corrected: Reveal stated in dosFull[1].d and breakdown.late; the minion body-block stated in dontsFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.carry and phases[6].why. Real cooldowns (Heroic Swing 18-12s, Avengerang 9-5s, Comeuppance 100/85/70s, Karma E 10-8s) added to breakdown.cooldowns, which previously had no digit in it.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t advised adding anti-heal early "into his sustain".
audit.why: Dirty Fighting grants Akshan a shield every third hit, not a heal. Grievous Wounds does nothing to a shield, so the item advice was pointed at a mechanic he does not have.
audit.corrected: Replaced the anti-heal clause with penetration timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim under "RE + W the dive package"; dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim under "Shove past river with E down".
audit.why: Both titles promise a specific mechanic and the bodies discussed Mantra economy instead.
audit.corrected: Both replaced with bodies that answer their own titles, using Heroic Swing's 18s and Karma's E cooldown.

notes:
CHART: the full layer disagreed with both the content layer and the packet levelChart on five of seven rows. I moved the full layer onto the content layer's verdict (which the packet corroborates) and rewrote every why in the same proposal. Rows 0-3 and 6 therefore carry a full-layer side edit with no paired win[N] edit, because win[0..3] and win[6] were already correct — editing them would have created the disagreement, not fixed it.

DIFFICULTY: TRICKY / 7-of-10 against a 59.02% win rate was internally contradictory, so diff, tone, diffRating and both copies of the rating sentence moved to EVEN / 5-of-10. Akshan's carry threat stays high (7/10) because Comeuppance is a genuine cross-map pick tool; that is not the same as the lane being hard.

CONTENT whys[] INDEX DRIFT AGAIN: whys[3] read "Level 4" and whys[5] read "Level 6 remains his window too" while the labels are Levels 4-5 / Level 6 / First item. Same drift I found on akali — worth a repo-wide check.

GOING ROGUE NOT FULLY ASSERTED: the kit text for Akshan's W is truncated mid-sentence ("while moving towards Scoundr"), so the conditions under which he can enter camouflage are not established by the file. I stated only that Karma's W reveals him out of it, which the reveal flag and Riot's Focused Resolve text do support, and made no claim about when he can use it.

Unverified, so not asserted: whether Karma's W root knocks Akshan off Heroic Swing mid-swing (his text says he is knocked off by colliding with champions or terrain, which is not the same as being rooted), and whether the root can be cleansed or reduced by tenacity.
